brief: Maths Standard start (root request, 18 November 2026), methods of brief 243

syllabus: Mathematics Standard 11-12 (2024), Year 12 Standard 2 and Standard 1

officialEvidence.source: NSW Curriculum Year 12 Standard 2 Investment and loans and Annuities pages and Year 12 Standard 1 Depreciation and loans page, as recorded in the crosswalk (read 18 November 2026)

siteSource.note: Paths are repo paths at this commit, read from the read-only local clone C:/Users/kygs/teaching-app-fix at the same commit (not modified). SHA256 values recomputed from the clone on 18 November 2026 and match the crosswalk inventory. Investment and loans lessons 07, 08, 09, 10 and 12 and Annuities lessons 01, 02 and 03 use data-step-id sections; worked examples are we-1 and we-2 inside them.

recommendations: Run i12 to i23 in outline order. Standard 2 students take all twelve. Standard 1 students take i12, i13, i14, i16, i17 and i18, then go to math-s12-t01 (i15 and the Annuities videos i19 to i23 are Standard 2 only). i16 must open without i15, and i18 needs a final frame that serves both paths.

Joins: i12 opens on math-s12-i11's proposed final frame (a price tag with "buy now, pay later?"); this part proposes hanging it on the $3 000 e-bike of the site's BNPL table. Provisional until both designs agree. i23 hands to math-s12-t01 with a right-angled roof triangle on the house from i18.

Pace flags (gentler Standard pace): i17 is at risk (daily compound interest, a statement and minimum payments); suggested split i17a and i17b. i14 and i23 should be watched. The others fit 7 to 9 minutes.

Method: Standard 2 has no logarithms and no loan repayment formula. Repayments come from a table of repayments per $1 000 or a loan calculator; terms and amounts owing from a spreadsheet or a supplied graph; annuity values from future value and present value interest factor tables (generated to 4 d.p. in work/brief-standard-i2/factor-tables-output.txt). Credit card day-count interest is compound: I = P(1 + r/365)^n - P.

Money figures (root ruling 5), read 18 November 2026: RBA F5 October 2026 (credit cards standard 21.74% p.a., low rate 13.49%, banks' discounted owner-occupier variable 7.05%); RBA F8 September 2026 (credit card balances incurring interest 18.91%, new fixed-rate personal term loans 10.39%); RBA F4 October 2026 (bonus savings 5.05%, online savings 3.30%, 1-year term deposits 5.00%); Moneysmart on BNPL fees and credit card interest-free days; ASIC on BNPL credit licensing from June 2025 and the minimum repayment warning; ATO: super guarantee 12% for 2026-27 and Payday Super from 1 July 2026. Each video says once that rates change.

Fourteen new site findings are logged as MS-19 to MS-32 in docs/production/claude-pm/site-corrections-maths-standard.md (section 6): five numerical errors in lesson10 (MS-19, MS-21, MS-22, MS-23, with MS-20 the simple-interest method), one method finding across lessons 08, 10, 12 and annuities 02 (MS-24), three rounding errors in annuities 02 and 03 (MS-25 to MS-27), one in lesson12 (MS-28), three gaps (MS-29 factor tables, MS-30 credit card fees, rates, statement and goals, MS-31 withdrawal annuity) and one owner note on lottery contexts (MS-32).

Outline problem: the outline table puts Trigonometry (rows 37 to 47) straight after this strand, but the outline's recommended Year 12 strand order puts Ratios and rates (rows 48 to 61) before Trigonometry. i23's final frame follows the table (math-s12-t01) as briefed; root should settle the order.

Kit needs for i12 to i23 are in docs/production/claude-pm/checks/maths-standard-kit-needs-i.md (section "i12 to i23"); the main new parts are InterestFactorTable, ReducingBalanceTable and CreditCardStatement.
